scope: Formal and semantic audit of Steffel schiógameke / pamaguéameke against modern seyó-/siyó- blue-green forms

historical_evidence.source: Steffel as edited and analyzed by Merrill et al. 2020
historical_evidence.notes: Attested in the published dictionary; Brno manuscript has schiójameke. Merrill states that -gameke may be a variant of -cameke but explicitly cautions that participial segmentation is not certain in this word.

historical_evidence.source: Steffel as edited and analyzed by Merrill et al. 2020
historical_evidence.notes: A distinct historical green term. A connected-text variant pamaguéame lacks final -ke; Merrill analyzes this as evidence for optional use of the reduplicative -ke element.

modern_multivariety_evidence.source: Compendio básico de la gramática ralámuli, 1997
modern_multivariety_evidence.notes: The same source identifies siyó as a basic blue-green color root and documents regional sh~s variation as non-meaning-changing phonetic/orthographic variation.

independent_formal_controls.evidence: Merrill assigns historical <sch> the value [š] and documents initial alternations schiné~siní, schunú-cu~sunú-cu, schuguí~suguí-simí outside the target lexeme.
Caballero 2008 documents palatalization of Choguita /s/ before high vowels, including word-initial /suní/ and /si-méa/.

The 1997 multivariety paradigm itself documents e/i variation across regions in the target color root. This supports modern dialectal variability but is not treated as an independent historical sound law.
Merrill notes that all other basic historical color terms end in -cameke and that historical g~c alternation makes -gameke a possible variant of -cameke.
pamaguéameke~pamaguéame is directly attested inside Steffel's material, supporting internal alternation between an -ameke form and a form ending in -ame.

major_strengths: Steffel explicitly places schiógameke in the same blue-green semantic field occupied by modern seyó/siyó.
Historical š~s has independent controls in Steffel and modern Rarámuri.
Modern seyó~siyó and -kame~-name~-kami~-nami variation is documented across multiple regions.
Historical color morphology independently exhibits -cameke and internal -ameke~-ame alternation.
residual_problems: Historical schió- lacks an explicitly analyzed glide corresponding to modern orthographic y in seyó/siyó; no general glide epenthesis is asserted.
Merrill explicitly states that it is uncertain whether the participial suffix is represented in schiógameke.
The relationship between historical -gameke/-cameke and modern -ka/-na + -me/-mi requires a dedicated morphological reconstruction.
pamaguéameke represents a competing historical green lexeme and should be studied as lexical competition rather than forced into the siyó lineage.

assessment.reason: The candidate now has direct historical semantic evidence, independent modern multivariety evidence, and external controls for the principal initial-sibilant and color-morphology differences. Remaining issues concern exact reconstruction rather than documentary independence or gross formal compatibility.

next_research_questions: What is the best reconstruction of the historical schió- versus modern seyó-/siyó-, especially the medial glide?
How should -gameke/-cameke be segmented relative to modern -ka/-na plus -me/-mi?
What is the historical distribution and eventual fate of pamaguéameke as a competing green term?
epistemic_rule: Grade A measures evidence architecture, not demonstrated cognation. Historical and modern morphology must remain separately analyzed until a correspondence series supports reconstruction.
